card.summary: H.R. 7148, titled the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, became Public Law No. 119-75 on February 3, 2026. This federal law provides funding for the Department of Defense, Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, as well as Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and related agencies for fiscal year 2026. It also sets guidelines for the U.S. Sentencing Commission, extends various healthcare, Medicaid, Medicare, and trade programs, introduces pharmacy benefit management transparency rules, and awards a payment to the widow of a late representative.

card.summary: H.R. 5304 provides federal fiscal year 2026 appropriations and sets policy requirements for the Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, as well as several related agencies. The legislation allocates funding for employment training, public health research and programs, elementary and secondary education, higher education student assistance, and various social support programs while also restricting funds for specific administrative rules, executive orders, and organizational grants.

summary: S. 2587 provides fiscal year 2026 appropriations for the Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services (HHS), and Education, and related agencies. It sets spending levels and includes specific requirements, restrictions, and policy provisions for various federal programs administered by these departments.

affected_groups.effect: Receive annual appropriations and must comply with spending limits, reporting requirements, and program restrictions.
affected_groups.group: Federal Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, and Related Agencies

affected_groups.effect: Receive formula grants and funding allotments for education, workforce training, health services, and public assistance programs.
Affected by funding levels for student financial assistance, including a maximum Pell Grant of $6,335 for award year 2026-2027, special education, and institutional support grants.
Impacted by funding allocations for medical research, public health programs, Medicare, and Medicaid administration.

key_provisions: Provides discretionary funding and sets rules for programs within the Department of Labor, including employment and training services, Job Corps, unemployment insurance operations, and worker protection agencies.

Provides funding and outlines requirements for HHS agencies, including the Health Resources and Services Administration, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Institutes of Health, Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration, and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services.

Appropriates funds for Department of Education programs, including education for the disadvantaged, impact aid, school improvement, special education, student financial assistance, and higher education.
Funds related agencies such as the Corporation for National and Community Service, National Labor Relations Board, Social Security Administration, and Railroad Retirement Board.
Prohibits the use of appropriated funds for abortions, except in cases of rape, incest, or danger to the life of the mother.
Includes general provisions restricting lobbying, propaganda, and certain federal regulations across covered agencies.
